 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for short), challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.8342/2010 dated 13.06.2012 by the XII Additional Small Causes Judge and MACT, Bengaluru,
seeking either enhancement of compensation or remanding the matter to the Tribunal.

entities.text: XII Additional Small Causes Judge and MACT, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The brief facts of the case are that the claimant has sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 17.08.2010 at about 1.00 p.m., on Jakkur - Amruthahalli Road near IPS Layout junction between the vehicles Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AB-2772 NC:
2023:KHC:24740 (offending vehicle) and motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04- EP-06.
Therefore, the claimant has preferred claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.

In the present case, the appellant has filed two applications i.e., I.A.Nos.1/2018 and 2/2012 under Order XLI Rule 27 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for production of additional evidence which are medical bills and hospitalization charges along with four discharge summaries contending that after delivery of judgment and award by the Tribunal, the claimant was admitted to the hospital for four times and incurred considerable amount towards medical expenses and hospitalization charges.
Also, it is submitted that the percentage of disability at present is to be assessed in view of aggravated circumstances due to the injuries and disability sustained.

Therefore, prays for remanding the matter to the Tribunal NC: 2023:KHC:24740 for fresh consideration since the records produced as additional evidence requires examination and scrutiny by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Along with I.A.No.1/2018 and I.A.No.2/2012, medical expenses and hospital charges documents are produced along with four discharge summaries.

For the purpose of considering this appeal,
these two Interlocutory Applications are allowed considering the additional documents annexed with the applications.

Upon considering these four discharge summaries, the bills, receipts of medical expenditure and hospitalization charges, they are required to be examined and scrutinized by the Tribunal by giving an opportunity to the Insurance Company for perusal of the same.

Also,
the percentage of physical disability sustained by the claimant as on today is also to be considered and evaluated, considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant as emerged in the present case.

Therefore, for considering these disputed facts involved in the case, the matter is required to be NC: 2023:KHC:24740 remanded to the Tribunal for fresh consideration in view of the observations made above.
Therefore, the matter is remanded to the Tribunal for fresh consideration.

6. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed.
ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.8342/2010 dated 13.06.2012, on the file of XII Addl.

Small Causes Judge and Member, MACT,
Bangalore, is hereby set-aside.
iii. The matter is remanded to the Tribunal for fresh consideration in accordance with law.

iv.
Liberty is reserved to the parties to lead oral or documentary evidence or both, if they are so advised.
v. All the contentions are left open.

vi. Parties shall appear before the Tribunal on 23.08.2023,
without expecting notice from the Tribunal.
The Tribunal shall decide the case and dispose of the matter within a period of four months from 23.08.2023, in accordance with law.
viii. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records along with certified copy of this order without delay.
